clue.text: Plots to send unwanted mail back

indicators.note: to send something back is to return it the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: spam is junk email nobody asked for

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to return junk mail to whoever sent it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to send ... back' turns SPAM round; 'Plots' looks like a verb (schemes) but is a noun meaning charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots in the surveying sense are charts or plans of land, which is what maps are.

clue.text: Ghastly, motor vehicle running into horse!

indicators.note: the vehicle runs into the horse, so it goes inside its name

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A grisly accident in which a car hits a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome and horrifying, much as ghastly does.

clue.text: Sound stand-in officer immediately following

indicators.note: sound signals that the stand-in's word is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a proxy acts on someone's behalf
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A trustworthy deputy officer takes over straight after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable but is the homophone indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means next in order, nearest, so directly following.

clue.text: Almost make mark on a city theatre director

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase's synonym is dropped

parts.note: to impress is to make a mark on a surface
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A theatre director nearly makes a name for themselves in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last S from IMPRESS, leaving IMPRES.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario is a theatrical manager or producer who stages shows, loosely a theatre director.

clue.text: Like swamps quietly captured by a Scottish queen

indicators.note: the quiet word is captured inside the queen's name

parts.note: Mary, Queen of Scots
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A Scottish queen is silently captured in boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy ground is boggy and waterlogged, as swamps are.

clue.text: One doing up army quartermaster's place on river?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a quartermaster runs the store of supplies
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An army quartermaster's depot sits by a river awaiting renovation.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorer renovates old things, doing them up to their former state.

clue.text: OAP makes peanuts, sadly, collecting info on song

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the rearranged nuts surround the other pieces
sadly means badly, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: gen is slang for information
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A pensioner earns a pittance by singing for information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' mixes the nut letters into SEPTUAN, which then wraps the information and song pieces; 'OAP' (old-age pensioner) is defined by example, as many are in their seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: An OAP (old-age pensioner) is someone elderly; one in their seventies is a septuagenarian, an example.

clue.text: Figure on plane, extremely rich old medic

indicators.note: extremely picks the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A wealthy elderly doctor on an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' means a flat surface, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a four-sided figure in plane geometry with equal sides.

clue.text: Superficial protégé determined to come first

indicators.note: the determined word is told to come first, ahead of the protégé's

parts.note: out to do something is determined to do it
a ward is someone under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: A shallow young protégé is set on getting ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward means external, on the surface only, so superficial.

clue.text: Apprehension that's unwarranted?

parts.note: apprehension looks like groundless worry, but means seizing a suspect, and unwarranted means done without a police warrant

explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary person may detain an offender without any legal warrant, the detention having no police authority.

clue.text: Head of Chambers more optimistic for staff

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of Chambers

parts.note: a rosier outlook is a more hopeful one

explanation.surface: The senior barrister at the chambers is feeling more hopeful about the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a set of barristers' offices in Britain, whose senior member is its head; here 'Head of' just takes the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosier is the hooked staff carried by a bishop.

clue.text: Back at college involved in football, say

indicators.note: one thing involved in another sits inside it, so these letters go into the game's word

parts.note: football is an example of a sport
being up means being in residence at university, in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone backs a student who is on the college football team.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to give them help and encouragement, the verb sense of support.

clue.text: Province Barbara Castle's initially identified with?

definitions.text: Province Barbara Castle's initially identified with?

parts.words: Province Barbara Castle's initially identified with?
parts.note: Barbara Castle, a British Labour minister, had the initials BC, which are also the standard abbreviation of a Canadian province

explanation.surface: A question about which region a British politician was linked with.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Castle was a well-known British Labour cabinet minister of the 1960s-70s; her initials BC are the postal abbreviation of the Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific coast province of Canada, abbreviated BC, the same as the politician's initials.

clue.text: Over the moon, no longer living in England's borders

indicators.note: the dead person's word goes inside the two border letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters, E and D of England

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed after leaving this life, somewhere within England.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for being thrilled, a close synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Potter's club briefly linked with another

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the golf club's name goes

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club
another golf club, a wood

explanation.surface: A potter's golf club, shortened, is attached to a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter's' is 'Potter is': Josiah Wedgwood was the famous English potter, and 'linked with' just joins the two clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah Wedgwood founded the famous English pottery firm, so he is the potter in question.

clue.text: Principal possibly stomachs rise of illegal drug

parts.note: stomachs are examples of bodily organs

indicators.note: in a down entry a rise reads upwards, so the drug's word is reversed

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: The head teacher, perhaps, has guts that churn at the rise of illicit drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal is a basic stop on a pipe organ, so it is one example.

clue.text: Super head — chapel, do we assume?

parts.note: the top is the head of something
a chapel, we assume, is not a church, and CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A senior figure wonders whether a chapel counts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's question plays on chapel being a lesser place than a church: NOT CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch means first-rate or excellent, an informal synonym of super.

clue.text: Dislike a retired vicar, getting no one's backing

indicators.note: something retired has drawn back, so the clergyman's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, the vicar's title

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so these combined pieces are read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A parishioner dislikes a vicar who has retired because nobody supports him.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike or distaste for something.

clue.text: Go astray in Bath, perhaps, having drunk this?

definitions.text: Go astray in Bath, perhaps, having drunk this?

indicators.note: the wrongdoing word goes inside the jumbled city letters
perhaps suggests the city's letters are taken loosely, arranged another way

parts.note: to sin is to stray from virtue

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether drinking this would lead them astray in Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' jumbles the city into ABTH before the wrongdoing goes inside. Bath is an English spa city, and the whole clue imagines the drink's effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a potent wormwood spirit, notorious for leading drinkers into dissolute behaviour.

clue.text: Creature found buried in Iron Age ruin

indicators.note: the letters lie buried within the run of words that follows, like a find at a dig

explanation.surface: Archaeologists unearth an animal in the remains of an Iron Age settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild ass of Asia, a creature.

clue.text: Monarch appearing in colour on very big screen

indicators.note: the monarch appears inside the colour word

parts.note: red is a colour
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
OS stands for outsize

explanation.surface: A king or queen is shown in colour on a huge cinema screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Rings Elizabeth for one kept in European city

indicators.note: the harbour is kept within the two ring shapes

parts.note: O is ring-shaped, and there are two
Port Elizabeth in South Africa is an example of a port

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a woman named Elizabeth held in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like a verb (calls) but supplies two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto, or Porto, is a city in northern Portugal.

clue.text: Thrifty spouse acquiring collar finally for boxer

indicators.note: the thrifty spouse acquires one extra letter, taken inside

parts.note: a sparing person is economical

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of collar

parts.note: a spouse is one's partner

explanation.surface: A careful-with-money spouse buys a dog collar for the family boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from 'collar finally' goes into SPARING, giving SPARRING; 'boxer' looks like the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparring partner is a boxer who trains with another fighter in practice bouts.

clue.text: Asian port and quay all British agents initially arrive at

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: British agents all meet at the quay of an Asian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport, on the Red Sea in western Asia.

clue.text: Most accessible shelter needing internal attention

indicators.note: internal means placed within, so the listening word goes inside the shelter

parts.note: a nest is a sheltered home
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: The nearest refuge needs some work done inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The closest thing is the easiest to reach, the most accessible one.

clue.text: Responded, showing hesitation about what players did

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the hesitation sound is read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
players are actors, who acted

explanation.surface: Someone answered hesitantly when asked about the actors' performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ER to RE; 'showing' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reacted is to have responded to something said or done.

clue.text: Both rather cultivated Rudolph Valentino, for one

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over, like turned soil, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Two people both rather refined admire the silent screen idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentino was the 1920s screen idol women swooned over, an example of a heartthrob.

clue.text: Work in university looking into surgical procedures

indicators.note: the college letter is placed looking into, so inside, the operations word

parts.note: ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: A university is studying surgical operations.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a work, especially a musical composition.
